note: Strategic digest of the last ~7 days, grouped by ongoing trend: leadership, splits and alliances, territory and routes, policy and designations, violence patterns, money. Routine seizures and minor arrests are left out. X posts are used only as sources. Verification: Confirmed = 2+ independent reliable sources; Single source; Official claim only. Status is shown only when sourced counts support it.

trends.title: Sinaloa civil war: Chapitos vs Mayiza
trends.context: The split between El Chapo's sons (Chapitos) and the Zambada faction (Mayiza), now in its second year, has spread from Culiacán to Mazatlán, southern Sinaloa and neighbouring states. It drives the highest sustained violence in Mexico and shapes who controls Pacific fentanyl and cocaine routes.

developments.text: Security Secretary García Harfuch confirmed that Navy forces killed Jesús 'Chuy' González Peñuelas, described as second in command of 'Chapo Isidro' and the Guasave Cartel and carrying a 5 million dollar US reward, after an attack on naval personnel; the strike falls on a northern Sinaloa group outside the Chapitos-Mayiza split, so federal and US pressure in the state now extends beyond the two warring factions.

trends.title: CJNG: regional commanders face parallel Mexican and US prosecution
trends.context: CJNG is Mexico's most widely spread cartel. Mexican and US authorities now build parallel cases against its regional commanders, while it keeps fighting rivals in Michoacán, Veracruz and the Isthmus.

developments.text: US prosecutions are reaching CJNG's cross-border support network, not only its commanders: a US court sentenced a Chinese national to 12 years for helping CJNG traffic drugs and launder money, and the engineer accused of designing a CJNG narco-tunnel into the US became the seventh person charged in the Tijuana tunnel case, where more than a tonne of cocaine was seized.

trends.title: Terrorist labels, extraditions and US scrutiny
trends.context: Since the US listed major cartels as Foreign Terrorist Organizations, allied governments have copied the labels and extraditions have sped up. The labels change the legal and financial exposure of anyone who does business with these groups.

developments.text: US sanctions on Sinaloa Cartel-linked people and companies are holding in Mexican courts: ZETA reports that sanctioned individuals and firms in Baja California sought amparo injunctions to unfreeze their bank accounts and were refused, so the US designation keeps their money locked inside Mexico's own banking system.

trends.title: Ecuador: Los Lobos vs Los Choneros
trends.context: Los Lobos and Los Choneros are fighting over Ecuador's cocaine export corridor, from prisons to the Manabí and Guayas coast. Inside the state, police and prison staff collude with the gangs.

developments.place: Guayas, Manabí, Los Ríos, El Oro, Esmeraldas
developments.text: Ecuador began its fourth curfew of the year on 1 November across five coastal provinces after 33 night-time violent deaths, and the armed forces reported 40 arrests in Guayaquil on the first night; a fourth round of restrictions in one year shows the coastal violence outlasting each earlier one, weeks before the elections.
